name: Git
summary: The agent's working files live in a git repository, and changes are committed or snapshotted as the agent works. History gives checkpoints, diffs and rollback; branches or worktrees let parallel runs work on separate copies. Some tools keep a separate shadow repository so the user's own git history is untouched.
how: Run the agent inside a git repo, or create a shadow repo for its workspace
Commit or snapshot after each edit or at turn boundaries
Use diffs to review what the agent changed
Roll back by restoring an earlier commit or snapshot
Give parallel agents their own branch or worktree
facts: Commits each edit with a generated message; /undo discards the last change
Shadow repo of tree objects at turn boundaries; never writes commits
Full history and diffs, but built for text files and adds commit noise
goodFor: Undo and review of agent edits
Parallel work on branches or worktrees
watchOut: Auto-commits can clutter the user's history unless a shadow repo is used
Large binary files and datasets fit poorly
Captures files, not the conversation; pair it with a transcript store
